page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfg6.10xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 3.1 GHz. It features 40 physical cores with a single thread per core configuration, providing 40 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.8 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and network-based resources. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. The dedicated Intel processor achieves a PassMark CPU score of 34,691.95 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 12,045.0. Memory performance is characterized by a cached read-only bandwidth of 2,133.36 GB/sec, which drops to 108.89 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. In database operations, the instance handles 34.78 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 14,249.04 on PassMark database tests. For specialized tasks, it demonstrates a software compilation score of 28,733.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 166.28 GB/sec. Large language model inference on a small 135M model reaches 1,841.39 tokens/sec for prompt processing, while a medium 7B model processes prompts at 56.94 tokens/sec.

The lack of local storage and GPU hardware represents a clear tradeoff, requiring external storage solutions and limiting its suitability for heavy parallel graphics processing or large-scale deep learning training. However, the dedicated core allocation and high clock speed provide stable, predictable compute performance. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high resource density of 40 dedicated physical cores paired with 192.0 GB of RAM offers a balanced profile for compute-heavy applications without the overhead of hyperthreading. This configuration is well-suited for workloads such as database operations, software compilation, web serving, and medium-scale CPU-based inference tasks.
